texts:
Put your phone in the cradle, open Drive, and your agent rides along.

The page starts in Driving: a face, a voice, four controls, and no keyboard. Hold Talk and speak. The reply comes back in one or two short sentences, spoken in full and clamped to two lines on screen. Park, and Type unlocks. Night is the default, because a bright panel at speed is glare.
It is the same talk loop the site already runs (mic, transcript, reply, voice, lip sync on a rigged avatar), sized for a car panel. Runs on a head unit browser or a phone in a cradle: three.ws/drive
"Repeat that", "stop talking", "louder" and "night mode" are answered by the page itself, with no round trip to a server.

Put your phone in the cradle, open Drive, and your agent rides along.

The page starts in Driving: a face, a voice, four controls, and no keyboard. Hold Talk and speak. The reply comes back in one or two short sentences, spoken in full and clamped to two lines on screen. Park, and Type unlocks. Night is the default, because a bright panel at speed is glare.

It is the same talk loop the platform already runs (mic, transcript, reply, voice, lip sync on a rigged avatar), sized for a car panel. Runs on a head unit browser or a phone in a cradle: three.ws/drive
Local commands like repeat, stop talking, and night mode are answered by the page itself, with no round trip to a server.
altText: Room-dark car interface showing a stylized 3D agent with headphones beside a large Talk button and four controls: Hands free, Repeat, Stop, Type.
Typing screen labeled Type with an input field reading Ask your agent something and a Send button, available when parked.
The agent mid-reply in Parked mode with the question What should I listen to on a long drive? and a clamped two-line answer on screen.

Also tighten the third post: the specific quoted command phrases were never verified, so either add evidence for them or state only the verified fact that local commands are answered by the page itself.
